key_insight: Scaling a test-time verifier (a model that evaluates candidate actions) reduces the intention–action gap in vision-language-action tasks more effectively than proportionally scaling the policy model itself. A larger verifier can reliably detect and select better actions from a policy’s outputs at test time.
problem_solved: Addresses misalignment between natural-language instructions and generated actions in embodied agents by reducing incorrect or unsafe actions without solely relying on larger policy models.
method: Empirically characterize test-time scaling laws for embodied instruction following to quantify how verifier size affects alignment.
Use a separate verifier to score/rank candidate action sequences produced by a policy at test time (rescoring, reject/accept, or selection of top candidates).
Compare resource allocation strategies (scale policy vs. scale verifier) and demonstrate that scaling verification yields higher instruction-action alignment per compute.
impact: Shows practitioners a more compute-efficient strategy to improve instruction-following and safety: invest in verification at test time rather than only enlarging the policy. This enables modular, scalable pipelines for aligned VLA systems.
visual_elements: Scaling-law plot: alignment/error rate vs. model size for policy-only vs. verifier-enhanced setups.
Pipeline diagram: policy generates candidate actions → verifier scores/ranks → final action selected.
Bar chart: alignment improvement per unit compute when scaling verifier vs. scaling policy.
Before/after example: instruction, policy-chosen action (misaligned), and verifier-selected action (aligned).
paper_title: Scaling Verification Can Be More Effective than Scaling Policy Learning for Vision-Language-Action Alignment
paper_authors: Jacky Kwok, Xilun Zhang, Mengdi Xu, Yuejiang Liu, Azalia Mirhoseini
